issues.legal_issue: Revision jurisdiction under the canal statute is confined to revision of a scheme approved by the Divisional Canal Officer.
material_facts: Applicants sought to shift the heads of watercourses, and the District Canal Officer rejected their applications.
The Superintending Canal Officer allowed revisions and ordered the shifts, although no scheme had been approved by the Divisional Canal Officer.
The High Court quashed those orders because the revisions were not maintainable.
issues.conclusion: The revisions were not maintainable, and the High Court was correct to quash the Superintending Canal Officer’s orders.
issues.legal_principle: Section 30B(3) of the Northern India Canal and Drainage Act, 1873 authorizes the Superintending Canal Officer to revise a scheme approved by the Divisional Canal Officer, either suo motu or on a timely application by a person aggrieved by the approved scheme. That jurisdiction does not extend to a matter in which no such scheme was approved. The Court relied on no earlier cases.

predicates.appeal_from_quashing_of_canal_revision: The proceeding is an appeal from a decision quashing a canal officer’s revision order.
predicates.no_approved_scheme_exists: The Divisional Canal Officer has not approved a scheme that is the subject of the revision.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a quashed canal revision and no scheme has been approved, the revision application is not maintainable.

issues.legal_issue: Applications seeking changes to watercourse heads amid competing interests may be treated as applications for preparation of a scheme.
material_facts: About 50 co-sharers sought to shift the heads of watercourses.
About 15 other villagers opposed the requested changes.
The applications were, in substance, requests that a scheme be prepared to change the watercourse heads or outlets.
The matter came before the Court in appeals concerning orders on revisions that the High Court had quashed.
issues.conclusion: The applications were to be treated as applications for preparation of a scheme and considered under the applicable provisions of the Haryana Act, with an opportunity for supplementary or amended applications and objections.
issues.legal_principle: The Court considered Section 30A(1) of the Northern India Canal and Drainage Act, 1873, under which the Divisional Canal Officer should consider the desirability of preparing a scheme in the circumstances. It directed that the applications be dealt with under Sections 17, 18, 19, and other relevant provisions of Haryana Act 29 of 1974, which had come into force. The Court relied on no earlier cases.

predicates.canal_watercourse_scheme_dispute: The proceeding concerns a canal dispute about proposed changes to watercourses.
predicates.multiple_shareholders_seek_watercourse_h: Multiple shareholders apply to change the heads of watercourses to meet their needs.
predicates.other_villagers_object_to_changes: Other villagers oppose the proposed watercourse changes.

issues.definition: When multiple shareholders seek watercourse-head changes in a canal dispute and other villagers object, the change requests are treated as applications for preparation of a scheme.
